gotchas: Q1 - THE FIELD STILL EXISTS, UNRENAMED: net.minecraft.client.Minecraft still declares 'private int rightClickDelay;'. It is set to exactly 4, as the first statement inside startUseItem()'s 'if (!this.gameMode.isDestroying())' block, and decremented in Minecraft.tick() by 'if (this.rightClickDelay > 0) { this.rightClickDelay--; }' placed after clientTickCount++/tickRateManager and BEFORE gameMode.tick(), pick() and handleKeybinds(). Bytecode (javap -c) confirms exactly three access sites in the class: putfield after iconst_4 at startUseItem offset 12-13, getfield/isub/putfield at tick offsets 35-48, and getfield/ifne at handleKeybinds offset 670-673. Nothing else in the game reads or writes it (it is private), so it is never force-zeroed on screen close, slot change, teleport, or respawn.

Q1 NUANCE - it is armed on ATTEMPT, not on SUCCESS: 'this.rightClickDelay = 4;' runs before any hit-result/hand/item logic, so a completely failed use (empty hand, PASS, FAIL, world-border reject) still costs the full 4 ticks. Conversely it is not armed AT ALL while gameMode.isDestroying() is true - startUseItem returns immediately, so vanilla re-attempts startUseItem every single tick while you mine with right-click held.

Q2 - CADENCE IS EXACTLY 4 TICKS (5 useItemOn calls/second at 20 TPS). The three lines that establish it: (a) startUseItem: 'if (!this.gameMode.isDestroying()) { this.rightClickDelay = 4;' (b) tick(): 'if (this.rightClickDelay > 0) { this.rightClickDelay--; }' (c) handleKeybinds(): 'if (this.options.keyUse.isDown() && this.rightClickDelay == 0 && !this.player.isUsingItem()) { this.startUseItem(); }'. Because the decrement is earlier in the same tick body than the '== 0' test, arming on tick N gives 3 on N+1, 2 on N+2, 1 on N+3, 0 on N+4 -> the next call fires on tick N+4. Period = 4 ticks, not 5.

Q2 NUANCE - the first press does NOT come from the hold path: handleKeybinds first drains 'while (this.options.keyUse.consumeClick()) { this.startUseItem(); }' inside the '!player.isUsingItem()' branch, and that path ignores rightClickDelay entirely. So a rapid physical click sequence can exceed 5/sec (one startUseItem per queued click in a single tick), while HOLDING is hard-capped at one per 4 ticks. A macro that fakes clicks via the click queue would be superhuman; a macro that mimics holding must use the 4-tick number.

Q3 - REAL ORDER INSIDE Minecraft.tick(), verified by decompile: (1) clientTickCount++ (2) level.tickRateManager().tick() (3) rightClickDelay-- (4) profiler "gameMode": gameMode.tick() -> ensureHasSentCarriedItem() -> ServerboundSetCarriedItemPacket if the slot changed  <-- SELECTED-SLOT SYNC (5) pick(1.0F) -> refreshes mc.hitResult (6) tutorial.onLookAt (7) profiler "gui": textInputManager.tick(), gui.tick() (8) if (gui.screen() != null) missTime = 10000 (9) if (gui.overlay() == null && gui.screen() == null) -> handleKeybinds()  <-- startUseItem / useItemOn HAPPENS HERE  then if (missTime > 0) missTime-- (10) gameRenderer.tick(); level.tickEntities()  <-- LocalPlayer.tick runs here; level.tickBlockEntities() (11) musicManager/soundManager (12) level.tick(() -> true) (13) animateTick, particleEngine.tick() (14) connection.send(ServerboundClientTickEndPacket.INSTANCE) (15) keyboardHandler.tick().

Q3(a) - handleKeybinds/startUseItem runs BEFORE LocalPlayer.tick and BEFORE applyInput for the same tick. LocalPlayer.tick is reached only via ClientLevel.tickEntities -> tickNonPassenger -> entity.tick(); inside it, super.tick() -> Player.tick() -> LivingEntity.tick() -> updatingUsingItem(), then aiStep() -> input.tick() and LivingEntity.aiStep()'s 'this.applyInput()' (LivingEntity.java:3094). Only after that does LocalPlayer.tick send ServerboundPlayerInputPacket and sendPosition() (Pos/Rot/PosRot/StatusOnly). Consequence for a macro: the ServerboundUseItemOnPacket for tick N is on the wire BEFORE that tick's movement/rotation packet, and before that tick's ItemCooldowns.tick() ('this.cooldowns.tick();' in Player.tick) and before updatingUsingItem() re-validates the held stack.

Q3(b) - handleKeybinds is strictly BEFORE level.tickEntities(). Q3(c) - the selected-slot sync happens TWICE relative to the use: once in gameMode.tick() (step 4, before handleKeybinds) and again as the very first statement of useItemOn()/useItem() itself. So as long as you go through MultiPlayerGameMode, ServerboundSetCarriedItemPacket is guaranteed to precede the use packet. If you hand-roll ServerboundUseItemOnPacket you lose that ordering and the server will resolve the use against the old slot.

Q3 EXTRA - mouse look is applied AFTER the ticks: Minecraft.run() does RenderSystem.pollEvents() then runTick(); runTick does processQueuedPackets(), runAllTasks(), then up to 'Math.min(10, ticksToDo)' calls to this.tick(), and only afterwards 'profiler.popPush("mouse"); this.mouseHandler.handleAccumulatedMovement();' before renderFrame. So rotation from real mouse movement lands between ticks; a macro that wants its rotation to be the one useItemOn sees must set it before tick() (or accept that mc.hitResult was computed at step 5 from the pre-existing rotation).

Q4 - VERIFIED REFUSAL CONDITIONS, in evaluation order. (i) handleKeybinds is not called at all unless 'this.gui.overlay() == null && this.gui.screen() == null' - any open screen or overlay suppresses the whole use path. (ii) if (this.player.isUsingItem()) handleKeybinds takes the swallow branch: 'if (!this.options.keyUse.isDown()) this.gameMode.releaseUsingItem(this.player);' then drains keyAttack/keyUse/keyPickItem clicks with empty while-loops - no startUseItem from the click path. (iii) hold path requires keyUse.isDown() && rightClickDelay == 0 && !player.isUsingItem(). (iv) startUseItem requires !this.gameMode.isDestroying(). (v) then !this.player.isHandsBusy() (true while steering a boat with a movement key held). (vi) per hand: 'if (!heldItem.isItemEnabled(this.level.enabledFeatures())) return;' - note this returns out of the whole loop, so a feature-disabled main-hand item also cancels the off-hand attempt. (vii) BLOCK branch enters gameMode.useItemOn; inside it '!this.minecraft.level.getWorldBorder().isWithinBounds(blockHit.getBlockPos())' -> InteractionResult.FAIL and no packet. (viii) performUseItemOn: 'if (this.localPlayerMode == GameType.SPECTATOR) return InteractionResult.CONSUME;' (ix) 'boolean suppressUsingBlock = player.isSecondaryUseActive() && haveSomethingInOurHands;' where haveSomethingInOurHands = !getMainHandItem().isEmpty() || !getOffhandItem().isEmpty() - sneaking with any item skips blockState.useItemOn/useWithoutItem entirely and falls through to the item's own useOn. (x) '!this.connection.isFeatureEnabled(blockState.getBlock().requiredFeatures())' -> FAIL. (xi) 'if (!itemStack.isEmpty() && !player.getCooldowns().isOnCooldown(itemStack))' else PASS - item cooldown blocks the ItemStack.useOn leg only, the block-interaction leg above already ran.

Q4 - WHAT DOES *NOT* GATE USE (three false friends from older versions/mods): missTime is attack-only in 26.2 - startUseItem has no missTime check (grep of Minecraft.java shows missTime only in continueAttack, startAttack and tick's screen/decrement lines). mouseHandler.isMouseGrabbed() appears exactly once in Minecraft.java, in the continueAttack(...) argument - the use path never checks it. Minecraft.isWindowActive() is never referenced in the tick/keybind path at all. Also note handleKeybinds is NOT gated by !this.pause.

Q4 - ATTACK-SIDE TRAP worth knowing if the same macro also attacks: 'if (this.gui.screen() != null) this.missTime = 10000;' and missTime is only decremented inside the no-screen branch, so the only thing that clears it is 'if (!down) this.missTime = 0;' at the top of continueAttack. Closing a GUI while still holding the attack key leaves missTime at ~10000 and attacks stay dead until the key is released.

Q5 - NOTHING slot-specific resets the use on the client. Inventory.setSelectedSlot(int) only validates isHotbarSlot and assigns; both vanilla slot-change entry points (handleKeybinds' 'this.player.getInventory().setSelectedSlot(i)' for keyHotbarSlots, and MouseHandler.onScroll's 'inventory.setSelectedSlot(ScrollWheelHandler.getNextScrollWheelSelection(wheel, inventory.getSelectedSlot(), Inventory.getSelectionSize()))') do nothing else. The cancel is generic and one tick late: LivingEntity.tick() calls private updatingUsingItem(), which does 'if (ItemStack.isSameItem(this.getItemInHand(this.getUsedItemHand()), this.useItem)) {...} else { this.stopUsingItem(); }' - because MAIN_HAND resolves through the selected slot, switching slots mid-use makes isSameItem false on the next entity tick and stopUsingItem() fires (LocalPlayer's override also clears startedUsingItem). Switching to a slot holding the SAME item does not cancel. rightClickDelay is untouched by any of this.

Q5 - the authoritative slot-change cancel is SERVER-ONLY: ServerGamePacketListenerImpl.handleSetCarriedItem does 'if (this.player.getInventory().getSelectedSlot() != packet.getSlot() && this.player.getUsedItemHand() == InteractionHand.MAIN_HAND) this.player.stopUsingItem();'. That class is only in minecraft-extracted_server.jar and is uncallable from client code; the client-visible equivalent is LivingEntity.updatingUsingItem() described above. Practical effect: a macro that switches slots while a bow/shield/food is being used will have the use cancelled on both sides without any explicit call.

BREAKING vs pre-26.2 #1: Minecraft.screen and Minecraft.overlay are gone. The screen-open guard is now 'mc.gui.screen() != null' / 'mc.gui.overlay() != null' on net.minecraft.client.gui.Gui (public final field Minecraft.gui). Keybind handling also moved partly to Gui.handleKeybinds().

BREAKING vs pre-26.2 #2: Inventory.selected is now private; use getSelectedSlot()/setSelectedSlot(int), and note setSelectedSlot THROWS IllegalArgumentException for a non-hotbar index instead of clamping. Hotbar width comes from Inventory.getSelectionSize().

BREAKING vs pre-26.2 #3: useItemOn returns net.minecraft.world.InteractionResult, which is an INTERFACE with record subtypes (Success/Fail/Pass/TryEmptyHandInteraction), not an enum and not InteractionResultHolder. Old 'result == InteractionResult.SUCCESS' comparisons silently stop matching; vanilla now does 'instanceof Success success' and swings only when 'success.swingSource() == SwingSource.CLIENT'. consumesAction() is a default interface method.

BREAKING vs pre-26.2 #4: useItemOn's return value tells you nothing about whether a packet was sent. startPrediction() sends the ServerboundUseItemOnPacket unconditionally; only the world-border check can prevent it. Anti-cheat-relevant: calling useItemOn in a loop emits one packet per call even when every result is FAIL. Vanilla's only rate limit is rightClickDelay.

BREAKING vs pre-26.2 #5: LocalPlayer.isUsingItem() is overridden to return the client-local startedUsingItem flag, while LivingEntity.isUsingItem() reads the DATA_LIVING_ENTITY_FLAGS bit. If you hold a LivingEntity/Player reference and call isUsingItem() you may get the server-echoed value; vanilla's guard in handleKeybinds is the LocalPlayer one. Likewise LocalPlayer.getUsedItemHand() returns the client-local usingItemHand, not the entity-data bit.
BREAKING vs pre-26.2 #6: isHandsBusy() exists ONLY on LocalPlayer - javap on Player, LivingEntity and Entity finds nothing. Common-side code cannot replicate that guard.

ACCESS: everything vanilla actually uses to throttle is private - rightClickDelay, startUseItem(), handleKeybinds(), continueAttack(boolean), pick(float). missTime is protected. There is no public API to read or reset vanilla's cadence, so either add an accessor/shadow mixin on Minecraft or keep your own counter (the snippet in 'usage' does the latter).

CAVEAT ON WHAT I DID NOT VERIFY: I did not run the game, so the 4-tick figure is derived from the three quoted code sites plus the bytecode access list, not from an in-game measurement. I also did not decompile ClientInput/KeyMapping's press bookkeeping beyond isDown()/consumeClick(), so I cannot say how many clickCount entries can accumulate in one tick at high frame rates.
